v.rationale: All three pass their own tests. With no Accept header they all return JSON 401, 403, 404 and 422 responses, and with debug off they all hide the 'No query results for model [App\Models\Order]' message. The ranking comes down to ability and ownership ordering, which I checked with one request per test (Sanctum's guard keeps the first token's user across requests in one test). impl-2 enforces abilities as route middleware and looks up the order through $user->orders(), so it returns 403 in every case where the token lacks the ability. Its only bug is the missing integer cast, which returns total_cents as a string after a form-encoded create. impl-3 has the best idioms and the best tests, but global binding runs before the ability check, so a token without orders:read can tell an existing order of another user (403) from a missing one (404). That cuts against the 'no data from other users' requirement. impl-1 has the same leak and adds a worse bug: abilities are checked with Gate inside the controller after FormRequest validation, so a read-only token gets 422 instead of 403 on POST and can use the unique rule to probe other users' references. Its tests mostly go through Sanctum::actingAs with getJson, so they miss these problems.
